content.text: Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.311/f4c003b475a5cc42c5e9c60098f16cc5/artifact-capabilities # Artifact runtime capabilities A published Artifact page can declare **runtime capabilities** — abilities the claude.ai viewer grants the page at open time — by passing `capabilities: {name: config}` to the Artifact tool. The control plane is the authority on valid names and config shapes. Declaration gestures: **omitting** `capabilities` on a redeploy carries the stored declaration forward unchanged (and preserves the artifact's stored contract pin); an **empty object** `{}` is the explicit clear-all; a **non-empty object** is a full-set declaration (anything stored but not restated is revoked). Moving a republished artifact's runtime version is a deliberate gesture — pass `contract: 'latest'` to upgrade, or a specific version to pin or roll back — never a side effect of editing. **A page that republishes itself** through the `artifact` capability sends its whole document in exactly the shape the Artifact tool publishes, so a later publish from the tool recognizes and replaces the skeleton instead of nesting it: `` — no whitespace between those tags and nothing else in the head — then the page content exactly as it was written for the tool (its `` and `<style>` first, inside the body, regenerated from the page's state), then `</body></html>`. **Available capabilities:** `artifact`, `assets`, `comments`, `db`, `downloads`, `files`, `mcp`, `room`, `sample`, `self`, `user` — the complete set of capability names you may declare; built in on every page, called without declaring (never pass these in `capabilities`): `permissions`. Anything not listed is unavailable to this user. > Tool spelling in this session: the `Artifact` tool's `action: "read_db"` / `"write_db"` with a `db_op` are the `ArtifactData` tool, whose `action` is that `db_op` ("get", "list", "query", "set", "update", "str_replace", "delete", "batch") with the other fields unchanged — load it with ToolSearch when you first need it. Read the steps below with that substitution. Runtime contract 0.2.91 Capability namespaces live behind `claude.use(name)`: `const db = await claude.use("db")` resolves the capability's namespace, or `null` when this view cannot run it (not served, not granted, or failed to load — indistinguishable by design). Branch on `null` and design for absence. `window.claude` carries only `use`: no `window.claude.db`, `.room`, or `.artifact` member is ever promised, so never read one — render the page without them and light features up when the promise resolves (later, never within your script's first run, and unordered with DOMContentLoaded; `null` after 10 s when no viewer answers). The resolved namespace is frozen and platform-owned: call its functions and keep the reference; never assign to it, `defineProperty` on it, or replace a member (wrap it for your own helpers). Permission stays on the calls: a consent prompt, rate limit, or policy refusal arrives on the first call, never from `use()`. Awaiting `use("db")` again is free (memoized); an unknown name resolves `null`. --- capability: artifact --- Use `artifact` for pages that should remember what people do with them: polls, sign-up sheets, checklists, trackers, boards — the page is the record; data kept server-side, or seeded or read back by Claude, is `db`. Declare `capabilities: {artifact: {}}`; `const artifact = await claude.use("artifact")`, then `await artifact.publish(html)` saves `html` (a complete document, doctype first) as the new version, and every open view, this one included, reloads to it. Nothing a viewer types, ticks or drags is kept unless the page publishes it. So embed the shared state as data in the HTML you publish and render the page from it; when an interaction completes, update the state, regenerate the document and publish it — never serialize the live DOM; batch rapid edits into one publish; publish only after a viewer acts, never on load. `conflict` is routine (every view reloads to the winner, dropping this edit): no retry. For read-only viewers publish rejects `not_granted`/`not_writer` — render a read-only view. --- capability: assets --- `assets` stores uploaded assets: `const assets = await claude.use("assets")`; `assets.upload(blob)` (image, SVG, video, PDF, font, CSS/JS, or CSV/Markdown/JSON/text; 20 MiB cap, CSS/JS 16 MiB, SVG 2 MiB and sanitized) resolves `{id, url, sizeBytes, contentType}`; `assets.list()` resolves `{assets, usage}`; `assets.delete(id)` removes one for good: only on a deliberate user action, updating rows that held it. Declare `capabilities: {assets: {}}`: only Editors and up get it, others get `null` from `use("assets")` (hide asset UI; handle errors). Only if the user wants uploads from non-editors, declare `{assets: {upload: "interact"}}`: where enabled, Contributors can upload but list and delete only their own, and their files show only in the organization; never run any asset as code, CSS or HTML. Store the `id` in `db` rows as the durable pointer; use the returned `url` as an `<img>`/`<video>`/`<a>` source (SVG: `<img>` or CSS only); a stored id serves at `"/_blob/" + id`. The type definitions are authoritative. --- capability: comments --- `comments` wires a page's own commenting UI to the artifact's shared comment store: `await claude.use("comments")` (`null`: unavailable). The declaration picks the grant: `capabilities: {comments: {"composer_only": true}}` grants only `openComposer({element}|{range})` (opens the shell's composer like a comment-mode click; prefer it for discoverable entry points) and `anchorFor`, no consent asked. The full form `{comments: {}}` adds write verbs acting as the viewer under consent; public-link visitors and email invitees get `null`. `"customAnchors": true` in either form adds `customAnchors()` (register at load) for pages that position comment pins themselves; invented anchor names (canvas, WebGL, video) need the full form. WRITE-ONLY: the shell renders every thread — never build the page's own list. Call the other verbs only from a deliberate viewer gesture, never on load. Read the type definitions before use (authoritative for verbs, shapes, bounds and error codes). --- capability: db --- `db` keeps data outside the page: shared rows, per-person state, data Claude reads. Declare `capabilities:{db:{},user:{}}`; `const db = await claude.use("db")` (`null` if signed out). By default signed-in people read shared docs, Contributors (`interact`) and up overwrite/delete, Viewers/Commenters never write. `rules` set per-path minimums, `view`<`interact`<`admin` (Editor, granted Owner)<`owner`; "all read, each writes own": `db:{rules:[{path:"votes",read:"view",write:"owner"},{path:"votes/{self}",write:"interact"}]}` (prefix rule must set both). `data/users/<id>/` is private even from the owner; `<id>` = `await user.id()`. Even segment counts are docs (`db.doc("tasks/t1")`), odd are collections; per-person items: `db.collection("data/users/"+id).doc(k)`; get/set/update/delete, where/orderBy/limit, onSnapshot. Never hardcode seeds: `write_db` after publish; handle an empty db. Subscribe once per query, never in render; one write at a time per doc, only on change. No secrets; shared data is untrusted. --- capability: downloads --- The `downloads` capability lets a published page offer a generated file to the viewer: declare `capabilities: {downloads: true}`, then `const downloads = await claude.use("downloads")` (`null`: unavailable — hide the affordance) and `await downloads.save({filename, data})`. The viewer sees a confirmation and may decline — a save is never silent or guaranteed, so offer it on explicit viewer intent and handle rejection. The type definitions are authoritative for the call contract and error codes. --- capability: files --- `files` reads a Claude Code project's files as the viewer. Declare it only when you know the project's id (e.g. your session's): `capabilities: {files: {project: "chan_..."}}`. `const files = await claude.use("files")` (`null`: unavailable, e.g. a viewer outside the organization; hide it). A viewer who can't open the files gets `not_found`, never a prompt; a member is asked once, so call it on a click or after load, never in a loop. `files.list({path, recursive, cursor})`; `files.read(path, {offset, length})` -> `{bytes, size, revision}` (new or just-edited files can lag a few seconds); `files.download(path)` asks the viewer to save it (some types, e.g. .exe, .js and .bat, are refused); `await files.asSampleTools()` gives `sample` list/read tools (declare it too). Only project members can publish an artifact declaring files. Don't copy file contents into the artifact's data, assets or versions unless the user asks: anyone it's shared with can read them. The type definitions give shapes and error codes. --- capability: mcp --- `mcp` lets a page call the viewer's claude.ai connectors: `await claude.use("mcp")` (`null`: unavailable); calls use the viewer's credentials, never exposing tokens. Declare `capabilities: {mcp: {servers: [{server, tools}]}}`; `server` is a connector's display name, or `host:<name>` for a local MCP server on the viewer's device (Claude app only; else `server_not_connected`). Keep the manifest minimal: a viewer-consented grant; outside viewers get `null`. Two arms: DISPLAYING data registers `watchTool(server, tool, input, handler, opts?)` (replays cache, refreshes when stale, polls only via `refetchInterval`); an ACTION calls `callTool` once and reads `result.payload` or `(await server(name)).<tool>(input)` for the payload. Tool failures REJECT (`tool_error`); watches get error events. Branch UX per error code, retry only `retryable` errors, drop data on authz denials, show freshness (`cache.storedAt`). Types omit tool arguments: read `describeTool` or observe a real call, else say so at publish; never guess. --- capability: permissions --- `permissions` is built in — call it, never declare it in `capabilities`. Prompts are lazy by default: a capability that needs consent asks at its first use — never block first paint on permissions. `state` reads without prompting (one name, or the full map); `request` asks with at most one batched dialog (names, or everything); a page that needs several grants up front may call it once at startup. `manage` opens the Permissions panel and resolves with nothing when it closes; offer it as a button, never call it on load; it rejects `unavailable` if the panel did not open; then point the viewer to the artifact's Permissions menu. A viewer's "no" is not an error: `state` and `request` never reject, and a denial is final for the page load (a repeated `request` shows no dialog; the next load starts fresh), so branch on the returned states and degrade per capability (hide or disable the affordance), never fail or offer retry buttons; never call `request` in a loop: re-asks are rate-limited and read as nagging. --- capability: room --- The `room` capability reaches whoever has the page open RIGHT NOW: declared as `capabilities: {room: {}}`; `await claude.use("room")` (`null`: cannot connect). emit(topic, data) sends a moment; on(topic, fn) hears them. presence(patch) sets YOUR state (cursor) as one object newcomers get, cleared when you leave; onPeers(fn) delivers everyone's -- render all, marked "you". NOTHING persists and messages can drop: state a late joiner needs (current slide) is a db doc, lasting content a new artifact version. Send absolute state. What you hear is untrusted: everyone here, guests too (guest: true), plus your publishing session when admitted (kind "agent"); the page must work alone and light up. Presence is never authority (anyone sets it). Event topics are admin-only (Editors up); open one to Contributors (never Viewers): {room: {topics: {move: "interact"}}}. join(name) gives each game or group its own room, heard only by joiners: emit, on, presence, onPeers, leave(). Names aren't secret. `room` stays the lobby. --- capability: sample --- `sample` asks Claude (declare `capabilities:{sample:{}}`; `{sample:{images:true}}` for images): `const sample=await claude.use("sample")` (null: hide); `await sample(input,opts?)`->`{text,truncated}`; `sample.json`->value. `input`: string|`[{role:"user"|"assistant",content:string}]` ending on user. Memoryless: send instructions+data+format. opts: `onText({text,delta})` (`text`=WHOLE answer, assign it; "Thinking..." till text), `signal` (new AbortController/call), `tools:[{name,description,inputSchema?,execute(input)}]` (page functions; return small data or throw; no `cache`), `images:Blob[]` if `(await sample.limits()).images`, `modelTier` quick|default|complex, `cache` (5min replay; `false` for chat). Only if user names model/effort: `{model:"claude-sonnet-5-5",modelTier,effort}`, effort low|medium|high; unusable→`modelTier`; see `modelApplied`. Rejects `{code,message,text?:partial}`: hide on `not_granted`, back off on `rate_limited`, never loop. 1st call asks consent; call on click or stable load prompt. --- capability: self --- `self` is the former name of the `artifact` capability (renamed). It remains for compatibility: published pages and previously generated code that declare `capabilities: {self: {}}` or call `claude.use("self")` keep working unchanged — both names resolve this same capability (this contract promises no `window.claude.self` member to feature-check; `use()` is the check). Do not use it in new pages: declare `capabilities: {artifact: {}}` and obtain the namespace with `await claude.use("artifact")`; see the artifact section for how to use it. --- capability: user --- `user` answers who is viewing this page and who your shared state names: the owner's organization and invited guests (`guest: true`); others are absent. `const user = await claude.use("user")`; `null` = absent (`user?.isOwner() ?? false`). `isOwner()`/`canEdit()`/`can(name)` need no setup (canEdit = admin level; `can("data.write")` = may write shared `db` docs, `null` = not told: keep the input; refused writes decide). Declare `capabilities:{user:{}}` for `id()`/`me()` (opaque id, comparable only within one scope; `me()` never null) and `profiles(ids)`; `scopes:["profile"]` adds names and `search(q)`; `["profile","email"]` adds addresses. Reads never reject. Store only ids (`id()` or `hit.id`), never a name, avatar, or Profile: names differ per viewer and go stale. Resolve in render, every time: `const ps = await user.profiles(idsOnScreen)` then `ps[id].name || 'Someone'` (cached: call again freely). `name` is `""` if unresolvable: use `||` not `??`. Call `search('')` on focus; set names with textContent. **Your connectors this session.** Connector tools appear in your tool list as `mcp__<connector>__<toolName>`. Set `server` to the `<connector>` segment — everything between `mcp__` and the next `__` (for `mcp__claude_ai_Slack_beta__search`, the `server` is `claude_ai_Slack_beta`). Copy the segment exactly, case included; when publishing, it is resolved to the connector's display name automatically. In the page's own `callTool`/`watchTool` calls, pass the connector's display name (its name as shown in claude.ai), not that segment — viewers resolve connectors by name only. The publish result states the exact display name for each segment it resolves; if the page's calls do not match it, fix them and publish again. Locally-configured MCP servers connected in this session can also be declared, as host servers: set `server` to `host:<server>` where `<server>` is the segment between `mcp__` and the next `__` in that server's tool names (`mcp__filesystem__read_file` → `host:filesystem`). Only servers from the user's MCP configuration count, with one built-in exception: `host:claude_browser` is the Claude app's own browser — declare it, with the tools the page needs from `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `preview_start`, `navigate`, `computer` and `form_input`, when the page must read or act on other websites; it answers only when the viewer opens the page in the Claude desktop app; the viewer is asked once, at the page's first call to it, and again at each click or key press that calls a banking or other high-risk site. The app's other built-in servers (`cowork`, `scheduled-tasks`, `session_info`, `workspace` and the like) are never host servers, and a page that declares one is refused at publish. A host server only answers when the viewer opens the page in a Claude app that has that same local server connected — say so to the user when you publish. The manifest's `tools` array takes the connector's upstream tool names (as returned by `listTools()` / `/v1/mcp_servers`), which can differ from the normalized `<toolName>` segment when an upstream name contains `.` or spaces. Every `servers[]` entry needs a non-empty `tools` array naming the tools the page calls — an empty or omitted `tools` list is refused and never means "all tools"; to publish without connector access, leave `mcp` out of `capabilities` (pass `capabilities: {}` to clear a stored declaration) rather than declaring an empty `servers` list. In hermetic/CI sessions where connectors aren't loaded but `$CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is set, fetch the list via Bash: `curl -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' -H 'anthropic-beta: mcp-servers-2025-12-04' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN" https://api.anthropic.com/v1/mcp_servers?limit=1000`; in that case use each entry's `display_name` as the `server` value (exact display names are always accepted alongside tool-prefix segments). **Call contract** (runtime contract 0.2.91). The platform-served `window.claude` type definitions for this contract are extracted under `/private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.311/f4c003b475a5cc42c5e9c60098f16cc5/artifact-capabilities`: `0.2.91/artifact.d.ts`, `0.2.91/assets.d.ts`, `0.2.91/claude.d.ts`, `0.2.91/comments.d.ts`, `0.2.91/db.d.ts`, `0.2.91/downloads.d.ts`, `0.2.91/files.d.ts`, `0.2.91/mcp.d.ts`, `0.2.91/permissions.d.ts`, `0.2.91/room.d.ts`, `0.2.91/sample.d.ts`, `0.2.91/self.d.ts`, `0.2.91/user.d.ts`. Read `/private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.311/f4c003b475a5cc42c5e9c60098f16cc5/artifact-capabilities/0.2.91/claude.d.ts` (how a page reaches any capability on this contract) and `/private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.311/f4c003b475a5cc42c5e9c60098f16cc5/artifact-capabilities/0.2.91/mcp.d.ts` before writing any code that calls the `mcp` capability — they are authoritative for this contract version over any remembered API shape. Open these files with the Read tool rather than `cat`: a file past the Bash tool's inline output limit does not come back in full. The type definitions cover only the call envelope, not a connector tool's argument names or result shape. Take argument names from the tool's input schema in this session's own definition of that connector tool, when it is loaded here. Learn a result's shape from one real call of a tool that is safe to run — never run a write only to learn its result. The published page may also read a connector tool's schema itself with `describeTool(server, tool)` at view time, once the viewer has allowed that connector for the page (viewers without that support reject it — treat any rejection as no schema available); this session cannot read that answer before publishing, so it is no substitute for a schema read here. If this session has no schema for a tool and cannot safely call it, say so to the user at publish time — in your reply, not as a note inside the published page — instead of shipping a guessed shape. Observed response payloads are the user's real data: learn the shape from them, but never embed the observed values in the published page as sample or placeholder data. ## Where a page keeps its state — this session - A per-viewer convenience (a remembered tab, a draft): browser storage; it never reaches other viewers or Claude. - The page itself is the record (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist): the `artifact` capability — a viewer who can write republishes the whole page from its state; every open view reloads to the winner, a concurrent save rejects `conflict`, and read-only viewers cannot save. Such a page regenerates the whole document from its state: keep the head, tokens and structure and change only the content. - Data outside the page (Claude seeds or reads it, more than the page shows, private per viewer, many writers at once): the `db` capability — documents under access rules, live through `onSnapshot`, kept across republishes. ## Verify before you hand over the link — this session A page whose `capabilities` you declared in this session gets one functional pass, not a render loop: after the first publish, one `ArtifactData` `list` of each collection the page writes, and, where its rules hide something from ordinary viewers, the same read with a lower `as_level`, which must not show what the rules hide from such a viewer. Then tell the user in one line what you exercised and what you could not. An Artifact made from an Artifact type is not such a page: its capabilities come from the type, and the type's instructions govern any checking.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/anchildress1/.claude/skills/gemini-prompting

Snapshot verified 2026-09-04 against <https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models>. Gemini API
names churn fast — `gemini-3.5-flash` went from default workhorse to legacy baseline in one
quarter. Re-check the docs before writing a model string, and always when the current date is
more than ~3 months past the date above.

## Models

### Text and multimodal (GA)

| API name | Tier | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `gemini-3.8-flash` | Flash | **Default workhorse.** Most intelligent Flash; software engineering and agents. |
| `gemini-3.7-flash` | Flash | Previous generation. Complex coding. Prefer 3.8 for new work. |
| `gemini-3.6-flash` | Flash | Balanced speed and multimodal. |
| `gemini-3.5-flash` | Flash | **Legacy baseline.** High-throughput only. Do not start here. |
| `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | Flash-Lite | **Fastest and cheapest.** Narrow classification, boolean extraction. |
| `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` | Flash-Lite | Frontier performance at lower cost. |
| `gemini-2.5-pro` | Pro | Hardest multi-step reasoning where accuracy outweighs latency and cost. |
| `gemini-2.5-flash` / `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` | 2.5 | Older line. New work belongs on 3.x. |

### Preview — text and agentic

| API name | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` | Advanced intelligence and reasoning. Pro tier — slower and pricier than Flash; justify it on the critical path. |
| `gemini-3-flash-preview` | Frontier performance tier. |

### Audio and speech

| API name | Status | API | Use it for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gemini-3.5-transcribe` | GA | `generateContent` | Speech-to-text with diarization. Batch. |
| `gemini-3.5-transcribe-live` | GA | Live | Streaming speech-to-text. |
| `gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` | Preview | `generateContent` | Low-latency TTS with expressive control. |
| `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` | Preview | `generateContent` | Controllable TTS. |
| `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts` | Preview | `generateContent` | High-fidelity synthesis — podcasts, audiobooks. |
| `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` | Preview | **Live only** | Low-latency audio-to-audio dialogue. |
| `gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` | Preview | **Live only** | Real-time speech-to-speech translation, 70+ languages. |
| `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025` | Preview | **Live only** | Real-time conversational agents. |

**Check the API column before you pick.** Models marked *Live only* run over the Live API's
stateful WebSocket session. They do **not** work with `generateContent` or `batchGenerateContent`,
and they are speech-**to-speech**: audio in, audio out. They cannot serve an asynchronous
request/response pipeline, and they cannot return structured text. Reaching for one in a batch
job is a rewrite, not a config change.

`gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` is the most common mistake here — the name reads like a
translation model you could call per request. It is a real-time conversation model built on
Gemini 3 Pro. For translating recorded audio in a batch pipeline, use a normal Flash tier with a
translation instruction and a `responseSchema`.

**Every TTS model is preview.** There is no GA text-to-speech id. Anything shipping TTS carries
preview risk — say so rather than implying stability.

### Other modalities

- **Image**: `gemini-3.1-flash-image` (Nano Banana 2) · `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image` ·
  `gemini-3-pro-image` (Nano Banana Pro, 4K) · `gemini-2.5-flash-image`
- **Embeddings**: `gemini-embedding-001` (text) · `gemini-embedding-2-preview` (multimodal —
  text, images, video, audio, PDFs)
- **Video**: `gemini-omni-1.1-flash` (GA) · `veo-3.1-generate-preview` ·
  `veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview`
- **Music**: `lyria-3.5` · `lyria-3-clip-preview` · `lyria-3-pro-preview` · `lyria-realtime-exp`
- **Agents (preview)**: `gemini-2.5-computer-use-preview-10-2025` ·
  `deep-research-preview-04-2026` · `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026` ·
  `antigravity-preview-05-2026` · `gemini-robotics-er-2-preview` ·
  `gemini-robotics-er-1.6-preview`

### Never use — shut down or deprecated

`gemini-2.0-flash` · `gemini-2.0-flash-lite` · `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview` ·
`gemini-3-pro-preview` · `imagen-4.0-generate`

### SDK

- **`@google/genai` v2.0.0+**. Pin v2+; the Interactions API broke at v2. Latest 2.21.0.
- `ai.models.generateContent({ model, contents, config })`
- Construct the client server-side only. An API key in browser-reachable code is a leaked key.
- Flash supports Search grounding, Maps grounding, File Search, Code Execution, URL Context,
  and standard function calling.

## Tier selection

Two capability levers: **model** and **thinking level**. Pull both deliberately.

- Smarter (harder reasoning, more reliable tool use) → higher tier and/or higher thinking.
- **Split a multi-call pipeline by job.** Narrow boolean classification belongs on Flash-Lite;
  the one call doing real extraction or transformation belongs on `gemini-3.8-flash`. Running
  every call at the top tier buys latency and cost, not accuracy.
- **Less** optimal (sub-optimal persona, "play like a beginner", looser output) → Flash-Lite
  and/or `MINIMAL` thinking. A bigger model optimizes *harder*; reaching for Pro to make
  something play dumber moves the wrong way. The prompt (negative constraints + few-shot) is
  the primary lever; the smaller tier reinforces it.

## Prompting Flash

Flash 3.5 favors directness over verbosity, logic over persuasion. The prompt is a control
surface, not a conversation. Chain-of-thought prose in the prompt hurts — move reasoning to
the thinking level.

**Structure**

- XML tags **or** markdown headers, never both — mixing muddies the instruction/data boundary.
- Order: `role → instructions → constraints → output`.
- Role + behavioral constraints go in `systemInstruction`. It persists across turns, so each
  user turn carries only the immediate task.
- Data first, task/question **last**. Bridge with "Based on the information above, …".

**Negative constraints** — state them explicitly, placed next to the instruction they guard,
not in a far-off rules dump. Plain and direct ("Do NOT reach for the most-efficient question")
beats hedging.

**Few-shot** — 2–3 examples are the strongest lever for style, persona, and format; stronger
than describing the behavior in prose. Match example complexity to the real task. For a
persona, *show* one turn of it.

**Thinking level** — set `thinkingConfig: { thinkingLevel }`, never "think step by step" in
the prompt.

- `MINIMAL` — fast; also stops a capable model from over-reasoning into behavior you did not
  want (optimal play when you asked for casual).
- `MEDIUM` / `HIGH` — genuine multi-step reasoning where accuracy beats speed.

Replacing verbose CoT prompting with a raised thinking level is a strict improvement. Delete
the CoT.

**Temperature** — 1.0 default. Lower only for deterministic extraction/classification.

**Structured output** — anything beyond trivial JSON gets a `responseSchema` (types, `enum`,
`propertyOrdering`) plus `responseMimeType: 'application/json'`. The schema enforces shape, so
stop babysitting it in prose. Still re-validate the parsed object in code: schema-valid and
semantically wrong is reachable, and a model response is untrusted input.

## Template

```
<role>You are [persona] doing [task]. [One line on how it reasons.]</role>

<how_you_work>
- [Imperative steps, one trait/action each.]
</how_you_work>

<never>
- [Explicit negative constraints, each next to the behavior it guards.]
</never>

<examples>
- [1–3 short worked examples that show the desired behavior/persona/format.]
</examples>

<output>[What to return; pair with a responseSchema for JSON.]</output>
```

`config`: `systemInstruction` = the above · `responseSchema` for JSON · `thinkingLevel` per
task · `temperature: 1` unless deterministic. Data goes in `contents`, task last.

## Sources

- Models — <https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models>
- What's new in Gemini 3.5 Flash — <https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/whats-new-gemini-3.5>
- Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite — <https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.1-flash-lite>
- Prompt design strategies — <https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/prompting-strategies>
- Gemini 3 prompting (philschmid) — <https://www.philschmid.de/gemini-3-prompt-practices>
- Gemini 3 prompting guide (Google Cloud) — <https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/start/gemini-3-prompting-guide>

content.text:
Gemma 4 reads clean modern headstones as well as Gemini. Its one real failure is the two-person stone. These numbers come from a throwaway script in my scratch folder; the real `scripts/benchmark.ts` isn't built yet.

## Results (9 fixtures, same prompt for every model, one run each)

| Fixture | gemma-4-26b | gemma-4-31b | gemini-3.8-flash |
|---|---|---|---|
| chambers-2011 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| gonzalez-2021 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| guo-2025 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| hildebrand-iii-2018 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| hildebrand-jr-2015 | 3/3 | 3/3 | 0/3 |
| **holmquist-2024** | **0/6** | **0/6** | **6/6** |
| cunningham-1752 | 3/3 | timed out | 3/3 |
| ellis-1818 | 2/3 | 2/3 | 2/3 |
| illegible-marble | 1/1 | 1/1 | 1/1 |
| **Name and date fields correct** | **75%** | **72%** | **86%** |
| Average time per photo | 34.7 s | 55.0 s | 14.5 s |

A score like 3/3 counts name, birth date and death date for each person. `illegible-marble` scores 1/1 when the model correctly reports no legible person.

## What the misses actually are
- **Holmquist (two people on one stone):** both Gemma models read every date correctly. They left the shared surname "HOLMQUIST" (carved once at the top) off both names. Gemini attached it to both names correctly.
- **Ellis:** all three models read 1818 as **1848**. I zoomed in on the stone and it clearly says 1818, so the answer key stands. This is a real misread by every model.
- **Hildebrand Jr, Gemini:** it wrote "LE ROY" for "LEROY". Its dates were right, but my scoring zeroes a person whose name doesn't match.
- **Timeout:** `gemma-4-31b-it` spent more than 4 minutes on the colonial Cunningham slate and was cut off.
- **Full-text accuracy is about 94% for all three models.** Holmquist pulls it down: the models read the two columns in a different order than my answer key.

## Scoring decisions you should know about
- Names are matched ignoring capitalisation and punctuation. Models write names in capitals as carved; the answer key uses normal capitalisation.
- "Mr" is ignored, so "M.r ANDREW CUNNINGHAM" counts as a match.
- Chinese characters in a name are ignored, so "郭俊士 Jiunn-Shih Guo" matches "Jiunn-Shih Guo".
- These are my choices. They should become explicit rules in the real benchmark.

## What this means
- **Two-person stones:** this is the requirement to adjust if we stay on Gemma, unless a prompt change fixes the shared surname. Gemini handles them; Gemma doesn't.
- **Speed:** the faster Gemma model (26B) takes about 35 s per photo against Gemini's 15 s. That's slow for a live phone flow.

The raw answers are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-anchildress1-git-personal-gravespeaker/a78fbb29-c412-483a-b679-0722adb27f13/scratchpad/bench/results.json`.

"""Rescore saved model answers: case/punctuation-insensitive names, honorifics and non-Latin script ignored."""
import json, re, sys
from collections import defaultdict

manifest = {e["file"]: e for e in json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))}
skip = set(sys.argv[2].split(",")) if sys.argv[2] else set()
rows = [x for p in sys.argv[3:] for x in json.load(open(p)) if x["file"] not in skip]


def toks(s):
    t = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]+", " ", (s or "").lower().replace("m.r", "mr")).split()
    return [x for x in t if x not in {"mr", "mrs", "miss", "dr"}]


agg = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))
cells = {}
for x in rows:
    f, a = manifest[x["file"]], agg[x["model"]]
    a["calls"] += 1
    a["ms"] += x["ms"]
    if x.get("error"):
        a["errors"] += 1
        cells[(x["file"], x["model"])] = "timeout" if "Timeout" in x["error"] else "error"
        continue
    a["text"] += x["text"]
    got = list(x["got"].get("people") or [])
    if not f["people"]:
        ok = 0 if got else 1
        a["fields"] += ok
        a["total"] += 1
        cells[(x["file"], x["model"])] = f"{ok}/1"
        continue
    c = t = 0
    for p in f["people"]:
        q = next((q for q in got if toks(q.get("name")) == toks(p["name"])), None)
        if q:
            got.remove(q)
        for k in ("name", "born", "died"):
            t += 1
            c += bool(q) and (k == "name" or (q.get(k) or None) == (p[k] or None))
    a["fields"] += c
    a["total"] += t
    cells[(x["file"], x["model"])] = f"{c}/{t}"

models = list(agg)
files = [fn for fn in manifest if fn not in skip]
print("| Fixture | " + " | ".join(models) + " |")
print("|---|" + "---|" * len(models))
for fn in files:
    print(f"| {fn.removesuffix('.jpg')} | " + " | ".join(cells.get((fn, m), "-") for m in models) + " |")
print("| **Fields correct** | " + " | ".join(f"**{int(a['fields'])}/{int(a['total'])} ({a['fields']/a['total']:.0%})**" for a in agg.values()) + " |")
print("| Text similarity | " + " | ".join(f"{a['text']/(a['calls']-a['errors']):.1%}" for a in agg.values()) + " |")
print("| Timeouts | " + " | ".join(str(int(a["errors"])) for a in agg.values()) + " |")
print("| Avg time per photo | " + " | ".join(f"{a['ms']/a['calls']/1000:.1f} s" for a in agg.values()) + " |")

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

**Project:** Gravespeaker, an MVP for Hacktoberfest 2026 "Ghost in the Machine". Hard deadline: 2026-10-31 23:59 PDT. Today is 2026-10-27.

- Repo: `/Users/anchildress1/git_personal/gravespeaker`. SvelteKit, Node 26.12.1, pnpm 11.28.9, Mastra, Gemma 4 through the Gemini API, Cloud Run deploy.

**Requests over the session:**

3. Disallow famous people in fixtures.
4. Find a pre-1900 illegible stone; set cutoff 2010; make atomic commits as you go; add `.semgrepignore`; remove `archbald-tomb`; focus on modern graves.

8. "run the benchmark now".
9. **LATEST (in progress), verbatim:**

   - "note: the code must use mastra properly to retry as needed and handle errors. this is a given anyway"
   - "holmquist which was a dual tombstone is now a non-goal. add TTD for v2 to the PRD that says we can tune the prompts then for that scenario"

Could we use render or digital ocean? if yes, test smaller gemma locally. this kills our open model requirement if flash is honestly that much better. only diff is that open ones are free with gemini key?? ground in a search."
   - "we need a deterministic layer in the code that parses names, strips/normalizes dates."
   - "languages other than english are also a non-goal for now, do not code against but we will not optimize for them"

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **GitHub spec-kit v1.2.3**, installed via `uvx --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git@v1.2.3 specify init --here --force --integration claude --script sh --non-interactive --ignore-agent-tools`. Skills: `/speckit-specify` → `/speckit-plan` → `/speckit-tasks` → `/speckit-implement`.
- **Gemini API models available with the project key:**
  - Hosted Gemma: only `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` and `gemma-4-31b-it`. No smaller hosted Gemma.
  - Closed comparison model: `gemini-3.8-flash`.
- **Gemma 4 family:** E2B, E4B, 26B A4B (3.8B active), 31B dense, and 12B Unified (added June 2026).
- **Pricing (official page, fetched):**
  - Gemma 4: free tier "Free of charge"; paid tier "Not available". So production runs on free-tier rate limits, and Google uses free-tier data to improve its products.
  - gemini-3.8-flash paid: $0.75 input / $3.75 output per 1M tokens through 2026-12-31.
- **Cloud Run DOES support GPUs:** NVIDIA L4 is GA with no quota request and 3 GPUs auto-granted. This contradicts the user's premise and must be pushed back on.
- **Render / DigitalOcean:** the search returned nothing usable.
- **Local hardware:** Apple M4 Max with 36 GB. Ollama 0.40.11 already has `gemma4:26b` and `gemma4:12b`; `llama-server` is also installed.
- **SerpApi:**
  - Google engine supports the `site:` operator.
  - Facebook Profile API needs `profile_id` (no name search).
  - An Instagram Profile engine exists. No LinkedIn engine.
- **Wikimedia Commons:** API used for CC-licensed fixtures; Wikipedia API used for notability checks.
- **Artifact** with `db` + `user` capabilities, used for the review page.

## 3. Files and Code Sections

**Branch `chore/speckit-setup`** (unpushed):
- `e4bcc9e` build: install GitHub spec-kit 1.2.3 with the Claude integration. Adds `.claude/skills/speckit-*`, `.specify/`, and `/.specify/` in `.prettierignore` (its manifests hash the generated files).
- `57c2b57` docs: ratify the Gravespeaker spec-kit constitution (`.specify/memory/constitution.md`).
  - Gates: MVP scope, never fabricate history, never silently merge identities, two seams only, behavior-driven tests.
  - Defers to CLAUDE.md and the PRD.
- `e346e3a` docs: limit agent output to what the user must act on. Adds a `## Output` section to CLAUDE.md:
  ```
  ## Output
  - The user designs; you implement. Report only what the user must act on or must know changed in the repo.
  - Per change: file and one-line effect. No narration of steps, tools, or reasoning.
  - Surface blockers, decisions needed, and failures in full. Omit everything else.
  ```
- `a1e8487` docs: add social media search for recent deaths to the v2 PRD. PRD §10 entry "Social media search for recent deaths (key v2 feature)":
  - Death year 2010 or later.
  - Pew stat: social networking among online adults 50+ reached 42% in 2010.
  - SerpApi two-step: Google `site:` search, then the Facebook/Instagram profile engines.
  - No LinkedIn engine.
  - Profile hits go through normal identity verification.
  - Living people's details stay out; link, don't republish.

**Branch `test/benchmark-fixtures`** (current; from main; unpushed; history rewritten cleanly):
- `c1cc170` test: add 9 headstone fixtures with ground truth for the benchmark.
- `2810dd1` docs: set fixture rules for the headstone benchmark. CLAUDE.md Layout lines:
  ```
  - Benchmark script: `scripts/benchmark.ts`. Fixture images: `fixtures/`, ground truth in `fixtures/manifest.json`.
  - Fixtures never depict notable people (anyone with a Wikipedia article). Models already know them, which inflates OCR and grounding scores. Same-name namesakes are allowed and noted as identity traps.
  - Keep the fixture set small. Recent graves (death 2010+) are the baseline. Historic stones are a minority that stress-test reading, never the norm.
  - Ground truth is unverified until the user reviews it (`reviewed: true`). Never publish benchmark numbers from unreviewed fixtures.
  ```
  This branch's CLAUDE.md does NOT have the Output section; that lives on the other branch.
- `0a2fb9b` build: keep benchmark fixtures out of the Docker build context. Adds `fixtures` to `.dockerignore`.
- `138e1a1` chore: drop gitignore entries for hosts and files this repo never uses. Removes `.output .vercel .netlify .wrangler` and `!.env.test`.
- `60e756e` test: mark the headstone answer key as human-reviewed.

**`fixtures/manifest.json`** schema per entry:
```
{ file, era: "recent"|"historic", difficulty: "clean"|"weathered"|"edge"|"illegible", text: string|null (lines joined by \n, [?] for unreadable word), people: [{name, born, died}] (dates "YYYY" or "YYYY-MM-DD", ? for unreadable digit, null if absent), source, author, license, licenseUrl, reviewed }
```

**Fixtures (9):**

|---|---|---|

**Benchmark scratch scripts** (not in repo), in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-anchildress1-git-personal-gravespeaker/a78fbb29-c412-483a-b679-0722adb27f13/scratchpad/bench/`:
- `run.mjs`: REST `generateContent` via fetch, temperature 0, same PROMPT for all models, `AbortSignal.timeout(240_000)`, writes results after each call. Scores text by Levenshtein-normalized similarity; people by name match plus born/died.
- `results.json`: the full hosted run.
- `run-local.mjs`: Ollama `/api/chat` variant (`think: false`, images base64). Models come from the `MODELS` env var; holmquist excluded.
- `results-local-12b.json`.
- PROMPT (verbatim core):
  ```
  You are reading a photo of a gravestone for a historical research tool.
  Transcribe ONLY what is carved or cast on the stone. Do NOT add, guess, or complete anything you cannot see.
  Return ONLY a JSON object, no prose, no code fences:
  {"text": string|null, "people": [{"name": string, "born": string|null, "died": string|null}]}
  ```

- Ellis: all three models read 1818 as 1848. Zoom confirmed 1818.
- Gemini wrote "LE ROY" for LEROY on hildebrand-jr (0/3 under strict scoring; dates were right).

**Excluding holmquist (not yet stated to the user):**
- Gemma 26B: 21/22 (95%).
- Gemma 31B: 18/19.
- Gemini Flash: 18/22 (82%).
- So Flash is NOT better; Gemma 26B leads. Speed is Gemma's only drawback. This contradicts the user's "this kills our open model requirement" premise.

**Local Gemma 4 12B via Ollama (holmquist excluded), raw strict-score output:**
- chambers 2/3 (likely a case issue), gonzalez 3/3, guo 3/3, hildebrand-iii 3/3, hildebrand-jr 2/3 (likely case), cunningham 0/3 with 1 extra (likely the "Mr" honorific), ellis text 0.74 and 0/3 with 1 extra, illegible 1/1.

# 🔬 OCR smoke test: Gemma 4 vs Gemini Flash

First pass at the PRD question "can Gemma read a headstone?", run on 2026-10-27 before any app code existed. This is a throwaway script, not `scripts/benchmark.ts`. It measures transcription and field extraction only. Grounding, unsupported claims and cost per run come later with the real benchmark.

## Setup

- **Fixtures:** the 8 human-reviewed stones in `fixtures/manifest.json` (5 recent, 2 historic, 1 illegible).
- **Models:**
  - Hosted on the Gemini API: `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`, `gemma-4-31b-it`, `gemini-3.8-flash`.
  - Local on an M4 Max (36 GB) via Ollama: `gemma4:12b`.
- **Settings:** temperature 0, one call per image, identical prompt for every model. Ollama runs used `think: false`.
- **Timeout:** 240 s per hosted call. No retries.

Prompt:

```text
You are reading a photo of a gravestone for a historical research tool.

Transcribe ONLY what is carved or cast on the stone. Do NOT add, guess, or complete anything you cannot see.

Return ONLY a JSON object, no prose, no code fences:
{"text": string|null, "people": [{"name": string, "born": string|null, "died": string|null}]}

- text: every line of the inscription in order, joined with "\n". Write "[?]" for a word you cannot read. null if nothing is legible.
- people: one entry per person commemorated. name exactly as carved. born/died as "YYYY" or "YYYY-MM-DD"; use "?" for an unreadable digit; null when the date is not on the stone. [] if no name is legible.
- A year that is not a birth or death (marriage length, erection date) is NOT a life date.
```

## Scoring

- **Fields:** name, born and died per expected person, each right or wrong.
  - Names compare case- and punctuation-insensitively, with honorifics (Mr, Mrs, Miss, Dr) dropped.
  - A wrong name zeroes that person's dates too, because an app can't attach dates to the wrong person.
  - The illegible stone scores 1 field: correct when the model returns no people.
- **Text similarity:** 1 − Levenshtein distance / expected length, after lowercasing and collapsing punctuation.

## Results

| Fixture             | gemma-4-26b-a4b-it | gemma-4-31b-it  | gemini-3.8-flash | gemma4:12b (local) |
| ------------------- | ------------------ | --------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
| chambers-2011       | 3/3                | 3/3             | 3/3              | 3/3                |
| gonzalez-2021       | 3/3                | 3/3             | 3/3              | 3/3                |

The results doc and PRD/CLAUDE.md changes are committed on `test/benchmark-fixtures` (not pushed), and `make ai-checks` passes. The local E4B run hasn't happened yet: the model is still downloading. I'll run it and add it to the results doc when the download finishes.

## Changes
- **`b20d8c8`** removes `holmquist-2024` from the fixtures and the manifest.
- **`d7dd56f`** updates the PRD:
  - Multi-person stones and optimizing for non-English inscriptions are now excluded from the MVP.
  - New v2 entry: tune the extraction prompts for multi-person stones then.
- **`bb2bfb5`** adds to the PRD and CLAUDE.md:
  - Model and search calls use Mastra's built-in retries and error handling, with no hand-rolled retry loops.
  - A deterministic code layer parses names and normalizes dates from the model output.
  - CLAUDE.md said "no retries", which contradicted your Mastra requirement. I added an exception for Mastra's built-in retries only.
- **`195c3c8`** adds `docs/benchmarks/2026-10-27-ocr-smoke-test.md` plus the raw JSON from every model, for the post.

## Results without the dual stone
| Model | Fields right | Avg time per photo |
|---|---|---|
| Gemma 4 26B (hosted) | **95%** | 24.5 s |
| Gemma 4 31B (hosted) | 95% | 50.1 s, 1 timeout |
| Gemini 3.8 Flash | 82% | 11.9 s |
| Gemma 4 12B (local) | 73% | 5.0 s |

**Flash is not better. Gemma 26B beats it, so the open-model requirement holds.** Flash's 86% earlier came entirely from the dual stone you just cut. On the rest, Flash lost points for splitting "LEROY" into "LE ROY"; the deterministic name layer would catch that kind of error.

## Your hosting questions
- **Smaller hosted Gemma:** none. The Gemini API only hosts `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` and `gemma-4-31b-it` ([releases](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/releases)).
- **"Cloud Run doesn't give me GPUs":** wrong. NVIDIA L4 GPUs are generally available, with no quota request needed ([announcement](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/serverless/cloud-run-gpus-are-now-generally-available), [docs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/gpu)).
- **Render or DigitalOcean:** not needed. Hosted 26B already wins, and the PRD rules out self-hosting unless benchmarks justify it. The local 12B result argues against it anyway: it invented the name "BETSEY BUCKS" on the Ellis stone.
- **"Free with the Gemini key":** yes, and that cuts both ways ([pricing](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing)).
  - Gemma 4 is free tier only; there is no paid tier.
  - The demo runs on free-tier rate limits.
  - Google may use free-tier inputs to improve its products. Uploaded headstone photos count.
  - Flash costs $0.75 per 1M input tokens and $3.75 per 1M output tokens.

## Failure every hosted model shared
- All three hosted models read Ellis's 1818 as 1848, confidently and without marking the digit as unreadable. That's the strongest argument for keeping the step where the user corrects the extracted fields.

The search turned up the official Google prompt-formatting page, plus several third-party guides.

**Official Google docs (ai.google.dev)**
- **System instructions:** The prompt template uses a system token, plus user and model turn tokens, with turns wrapped in start and end markers. Gemma 4 has no separate system field; the system message is a turn of its own.
- **Thinking mode:** Reasoning is switched on by placing a special control token inside the system instruction, and the model's internal reasoning appears in a dedicated channel.
- **Fine-tuning note:** For the 26B-A4B and 31B instruction-tuned models, training data without thinking traces can work better with an empty thought channel added to the prompts.
- **Structured output:** The official page covers function calling, with a dedicated delimiter token for string values inside structured blocks. I did not find an official page on general JSON output beyond that.

**Third-party guides (less authoritative)**

**Gaps:** The search did not return a release announcement or date for Gemma 4, so I can't confirm the release timing from these results. For exact token strings and structured-output syntax, check the official Google pages directly, since the third-party sites may be out of date.

result.output:
**Install**

The page gives this command: "`pip install litert-lm-api`". It also lists `uv pip install litert-lm-api`.

**Load a .litertlm model and set a system prompt**

The page shows the system prompt pattern and a multimodal engine setup. I adapted these into one example:

```python
import litert_lm

litert_lm.set_min_log_severity(litert_lm.LogSeverity.ERROR)

with litert_lm.Engine("path/to/multimodal_model.litertlm") as engine:
    messages = [litert_lm.Message.system("You are a helpful assistant.")]
    with engine.create_conversation(messages=messages) as conversation:
        response = conversation.send_message("What is the capital of France?")
        print(response["content"][0]["text"])
```

**Image + text**

The page does not document an image input class. Its only multimodal example uses audio, with `vision_backend` set on the engine and `litert_lm.Contents.of(...)` wrapping text and a file:

```python
with litert_lm.Engine(
    "path/to/multimodal_model.litertlm",
    vision_backend=litert_lm.Backend.GPU(),
) as engine:
    with engine.create_conversation() as conversation:
        response = conversation.send_message(
            litert_lm.Contents.of(
                "Describe this audio.",
                litert_lm.Content.AudioFile(absolute_path="/path/to/audio.wav"),
            )
        )
```

Check the API Reference for the image content class name.

**Sampler parameters (temperature, top_p, top_k)**

The page does not cover these. Its only generation control on `create_conversation` is `max_output_tokens`, shown alongside `thinking_config`.

**Constrained/JSON output**

The page does not cover this either. Check the [API Reference](https://developers.google.com/edge/api).

input.content:
"""Run 2 on a local .litertlm model. Same system prompt and sampling; the schema goes in the system prompt since LiteRT-LM has no JSON-schema decoding."""
import json, sys, time
from pathlib import Path

import litert_lm as l
from litert_lm import interfaces as i

model, fixtures, out = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
P = json.loads((Path(__file__).parent / "prompt2.json").read_text())
system = P["system"] + "\n\nReturn ONLY JSON matching this schema, no code fences:\n" + json.dumps(P["schema"])
s = P["sampling"]
l.set_min_log_severity(l.LogSeverity.ERROR)

results = []
with l.Engine(model, backend=l.Backend.GPU(), vision_backend=l.Backend.GPU(), max_num_tokens=4096) as engine:
    for f in json.loads((fixtures / "manifest.json").read_text()):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        row = {"file": f["file"], "model": "litert:" + Path(model).stem}
        try:
            with engine.create_conversation(
                system_message=system,
                sampler_config=i.SamplerConfig(temperature=s["temperature"], top_p=s["topP"], top_k=s["topK"]),
                max_output_tokens=1024,
            ) as conv:
                res = conv.send_message(l.Contents.of(l.Content.ImageFile(absolute_path=str((fixtures / f["file"]).resolve())), P["user"]))
            raw = "".join(c.get("text", "") for c in res["content"])
            try:
                row["got"] = json.loads(raw[raw.index("{"): raw.rindex("}") + 1])
            except ValueError:
                row["error"], row["raw"] = "unparseable JSON", raw
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - record and move on, like the hosted runner
            row["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
        row["ms"] = round((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)
        results.append(row)
        Path(out).write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
        print(f["file"], row.get("error", "ok"), row["ms"], "ms", file=sys.stderr)

content.text:
The hosted run is still going; results are in for the two local models. I'll write up both runs side by side when the hosted run finishes.

- **E2B (your local file):** 31% of fields right, and 3 of 8 photos returned unusable output.
  - It copied the shape of the format description instead of filling it in.
  - It invented "George Davison" for the Ellis stone.
  - Not usable for this app.
- **12B (local):** dropped from 73% to 55% of fields right with Google's recommended sampling.
  - Most of the drop is name formatting: "LE ROY" for LEROY, and "M." for "Mr". The dates on those stones were right.
  - Name parsing in code would fix those.
- **The Gemini API supports a system prompt and a JSON schema for hosted Gemma on our free key.** I tested both directly.
  - No other inference API is needed.
  - The blog post that said this needs the paid tier is wrong for our key.
- **The E2B runtime can't force JSON output.** Its forced-output setting doesn't take an arbitrary schema, so for E2B only, the schema went into the system prompt as text.
- **E4B is skipped.** You only have E2B downloaded, and pulling E4B takes hours.

## Your questions
- **System prompt:** yes, it's better. Run 2 puts the role and rules in the system prompt. The user message is just the image plus "Transcribe the gravestone in this photo."
- **Spelled-out format instead of structured JSON:** that was a mistake in run 1. Run 2 uses the API's JSON schema setting.
  - The schema describes each field, so the format instructions are gone from the prompt.
  - It still has to be checked in code: Gemma 31B passed the schema but still added a stray "```" after the JSON in a test call.
- **2026 Gemma releases:**
  - The full Gemma 4 family came out 2026-03-31.
  - Faster-generation variants of it came out 2026-04-16.
  - Gemma 4 12B Unified came out 2026-06-03, and isn't on the Gemini API.
  - Nothing newer fits this app. EmbeddingGemma 2 (October) is an embedding model, not a vision model.

Sources:
- [Gemma releases](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/releases)
- [Gemma 4 E4B model card](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E4B-it)
- [Structured output docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/structured-output)
- [responseJsonSchema with Gemma 4 (DEV)](https://dev.to/ai_made_tools/responsejsonschema-the-undocumented-gemma-4-feature-that-changed-everything-2obm)

# 🔬 OCR smoke test: Gemma 4 vs Gemini Flash

Two quick passes at the PRD question "can Gemma read a headstone?", both run on 2026-10-27 before any app code existed. These are throwaway scripts, not `scripts/benchmark.ts`. They measure transcription and field extraction only. Grounding, unsupported claims and cost per run come later with the real benchmark.

## Setup

- **Fixtures:** the 8 human-reviewed stones in `fixtures/manifest.json` (5 recent, 2 historic, 1 illegible).
- **Models:**
  - Hosted on the Gemini API (free tier): `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`, `gemma-4-31b-it`, `gemini-3.8-flash`.
  - Local on an M4 Max (36 GB): `gemma4:12b` via Ollama, and `gemma-4-E2B-it` via LiteRT-LM (run 2 only).
- **Calls:** one call per image per model, 240 s timeout, no retries.

| Run | Prompt                                                       | Output format                                         | Sampling                                        |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | One user message: instructions plus a format description     | JSON described in prose, parsed from the reply        | temperature 0                                   |
| 2   | System prompt with role and rules; user turn is image + task | JSON schema enforced by the API (`responseJsonSchema`) | temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64 (Gemma 4 model card) |

Run 2's full prompt and schema: [`run2-prompt.json`](run2-prompt.json). Run 1's prompt:

```text
You are reading a photo of a gravestone for a historical research tool.

Transcribe ONLY what is carved or cast on the stone. Do NOT add, guess, or complete anything you cannot see.

Return ONLY a JSON object, no prose, no code fences:
{"text": string|null, "people": [{"name": string, "born": string|null, "died": string|null}]}

- text: every line of the inscription in order, joined with "\n". Write "[?]" for a word you cannot read. null if nothing is legible.
- people: one entry per person commemorated. name exactly as carved. born/died as "YYYY" or "YYYY-MM-DD"; use "?" for an unreadable digit; null when the date is not on the stone. [] if no name is legible.
- A year that is not a birth or death (marriage length, erection date) is NOT a life date.
```

## Scoring

- **Fields:** name, born and died per expected person, each right or wrong.
  - Names compare case- and punctuation-insensitively, with honorifics (Mr, Mrs, Miss, Dr) dropped.
  - A wrong name zeroes that person's dates too, because an app can't attach dates to the wrong person.
  - The illegible stone scores 1 field: correct when the model returns no people.
- **Text similarity:** 1 − Levenshtein distance / expected length, after lowercasing and collapsing punctuation.
- **Errors:** a timeout, or a reply that isn't valid JSON. Errors score nothing and are left out of the field totals.

## Run 1: prose format, temperature 0

| Fixture             | gemma-4-26b-a4b-it | gemma-4-31b-it  | gemini-3.8-flash | gemma4:12b (local) |
| ------------------- | ------------------ | --------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
| chambers-2011       | 3/3                | 3/3             | 3/3              | 3/3                |
| gonzalez-2021       | 3/3                | 3/3             | 3/3              | 3/3                |
| guo-2025            | 3/3                | 3/3             | 3/3              | 3/3                |
| hildebrand-iii-2018 | 3/3                | 3/3             | 3/3              | 3/3                |
| hildebrand-jr-2015  | 3/3                | 3/3             | 0/3              | 3/3                |
| cunningham-1752     | 3/3                | timeout         | 3/3              | 0/3                |
| ellis-1818          | 2/3                | 2/3             | 2/3              | 0/3                |
| illegible-marble    | 1/1                | 1/1             | 1/1              | 1/1                |
| **Fields correct**  | **21/22 (95%)**    | **18/19 (95%)** | **18/22 (82%)**  | **16/22 (73%)**    |
| Text similarity     | 99.4%              | 99.3%           | 99.1%            | 96.6%              |
| Errors              | 0                  | 1               | 0                | 0                  |
| Avg time per photo  | 24.5 s             | 50.1 s          | 11.9 s           | 5.0 s              |

Raw output: [`run1-hosted.json`](run1-hosted.json), [`run1-local-12b.json`](run1-local-12b.json).

## Run 2: system prompt, JSON schema, recommended sampling

| Fixture             | gemma-4-26b-a4b-it | gemma-4-31b-it   | gemini-3.8-flash | gemma4:12b (local) | gemma-4-E2B-it (local) |
| ------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------- |
| chambers-2011       | 3/3                | 3/3              | 3/3              | 3/3                | 0/3                    |
| gonzalez-2021       | 3/3                | 3/3              | 3/3              | 3/3                | 1/3                    |
| guo-2025            | 3/3                | 3/3              | 3/3              | 3/3                | 2/3                    |
| hildebrand-iii-2018 | 3/3                | 3/3              | 0/3              | 3/3                | bad JSON               |
| hildebrand-jr-2015  | 0/3                | 3/3              | 0/3              | 0/3                | bad JSON               |
| cunningham-1752     | 0/3                | bad JSON         | 3/3              | 0/3                | 0/3                    |
| ellis-1818          | 2/3                | bad JSON         | 3/3              | 0/3                | bad JSON               |
| illegible-marble    | 1/1                | 1/1              | 1/1              | 0/1                | 1/1                    |
| **Fields correct**  | **15/22 (68%)**    | **16/16 (100%)** | **16/22 (73%)**  | **12/22 (55%)**    | **4/13 (31%)**         |
| Text similarity     | 99.2%              | 100.0%           | 99.4%            | 97.6%              | 20.0%                  |
| Errors              | 0                  | 2                | 0                | 0                  | 3                      |
| Avg time per photo  | 3.7 s              | 4.7 s            | 15.3 s           | 4.6 s              | 1.4 s                  |

Raw output: [`run2-hosted.json`](run2-hosted.json), [`run2-local-12b.json`](run2-local-12b.json), [`run2-local-e2b.json`](run2-local-e2b.json).

LiteRT-LM has no JSON-schema decoding, so E2B got the schema as text appended to its system prompt.

## What went wrong

- **Worn digits:** Ellis's 1818 was read as 1848 by every hosted model in run 1, and by Gemma 26B again in run 2. A zoomed crop confirms 1818. No model marked the digit with `?`.
- **Name formatting, not reading:** most name misses came with every date right.
  - "LE ROY" for LEROY (Flash both runs, 12B in run 2).
  - "LERØY" with a slashed O (Gemma 26B, run 2).
  - "M. ANDREW" for "Mr Andrew" (12B both runs, 26B in run 2).
  - Flash added the nickname "Eddie Boy" into Hildebrand III's name in run 2.
- **Gemma 31B's two run 2 errors were correct answers.** It followed valid JSON with a stray closing code fence. Both answers were right, including Ellis's 1818. Schema mode on the Gemini API doesn't stop it.
- **Gemma 26B listed a second person on Ellis** in run 2: "Thos. & Betsey Ellis", the parents named on the stone.
- **Local 12B invents surnames on worn stones:** "BETSEY BUCKS" (run 1) and "BETSEY BATES" (run 2) for Betsey Ellis. In run 2 it also returned a person named "[?]" for the illegible stone.
- **Local E2B is unusable:** without enforced JSON it echoed the schema's shape back. It read Ellis as "STIXIN George Davison", died 1878.

## The dual stone that got cut

`holmquist-2024` was a companion stone: two first names over one shared surname. It was in run 1 and removed afterwards (multi-person stones are an MVP non-goal, see the PRD).

- Both Gemma models read every date correctly but returned "MARSHA FOX" and "CHARLES RAY", leaving off the shared HOLMQUIST.
- Gemini Flash got all 6 fields.
- Including it, run 1's hosted scores were Gemma 26B 75%, Gemma 31B 72% and Flash 86%. That gap is entirely this one stone.

## Takeaways

- Gemma 4 matches Gemini Flash on single-person stones. The open model stays.
- Run 2 made hosted Gemma 6–10× faster (26B: 24.5 s → 3.7 s). It is now faster than Flash.
- One call per image at temperature 1.0 is noisy: individual stones flipped between runs in both directions. Scores this close need repeated calls per image before they mean anything.
- Exact name strings are fragile across models. Normalization belongs in deterministic code, not the prompt.
- Even with an enforced schema, parse model output defensively: strip stray code fences before `JSON.parse`.
- Worn digits get misread confidently. A user-correction step is the fix; it is deferred to v2.
- Small local models (12B, E2B) guess on worn stones. Hosted Gemma it is.

Run 3 scored the same as run 2: 12B at temperature 0 got 12 of 22 fields right (55%). Results are saved and committed, and nothing is pushed.

## Run 3 (12B, temperature 0)
- **Fields right:** 12 of 22 (55%), unchanged from run 2.
- **Speed:** 1.5 s per photo.
- **Same three stones fail the same way:**
  - Hildebrand Jr: "LE ROY" instead of LEROY. The dates were right.
  - Cunningham: "M. ANDREW" instead of "Mr Andrew". The date was right.
  - Ellis: an invented "BETSEY B. [?]", died 1810, plus a made-up second person.
- **Illegible stone:** it returns a person named "[?]" instead of an empty list.
- The temperature isn't what's causing these misses. They need prompt changes or the name and date code, so they're the targets for your prompt review.

## Commits
- **`19cef0c`** adds run 2:
  - Raw output for all five models and the run 2 prompt.
  - The results doc is now `docs/benchmarks/ocr-smoke-test.md`.
  - Run 1's raw output files are renamed to `run1-*.json`.
- **`ced8aa5`** adds run 3: its raw output, its prompt, and a section in the results doc.
- `make ai-checks` passes.

## Decision needed
**Do we tune on local 12B, or on hosted 26B?**
- Production runs hosted 26B, and it doesn't fail on 12B's stones the same way.
- In run 1, 26B read Cunningham right, and it never invented a surname on Ellis.
- A prompt tuned on 12B may not carry over to 26B.
- 26B now answers in about 3.7 s, close to 12B's local speed, so tuning on it costs little time.
- The catch is that it runs on the free tier's rate limits.

My recommendation: tune on 26B, or at least confirm every prompt change on 26B before calling it done. Your call.

## Config change for you to approve
- `tsconfig.json` doesn't cover `benchmarks/`, so the type check skips these two scripts and your editor flags red squiggles in them. Lint still covers them.

Run a 26B baseline first, then make one prompt change per run.

## 1. Run 4: baseline, no prompt changes
- Run hosted 26B with the run 3 prompt (system prompt, JSON schema, temperature 0).
- We've never run 26B on that setup; every run since run 1 has changed something. Without a baseline, no later change can be credited.

## 2. Run 5: list only the person buried
- In run 2, 26B added "Thos. & Betsey Ellis" as a second person. They're her parents, named on the stone.
- Modern stones do this constantly ("beloved son of…", "wife of…"). It's the one real misread the prompt can fix, and it matters for the post-2010 stones the app targets.
- Rule to add: list only the people the stone commemorates. Relatives it names in relation to them are not people.

## 3. Run 6: mark a worn digit instead of guessing
- 1818 read as 1848 is the most repeated miss across every run.
- Rule to add: "If any digit could be read two ways, write `?` for it."
- A partial date (`18?8`) hurts search less than a wrong one, and with field correction deferred to v2, a wrong date can't be fixed.
- If 26B still guesses, try thinking mode on this stone only. That costs latency, so it has to earn it.

## Leave these to code, not the prompt
These are formatting misses; the dates were right every time.

| Miss | Fix in name/date parsing |
|---|---|
| "M. ANDREW" | Expand "M." and "Mr" as honorifics, then drop them |
| "LERØY" | Map lookalike letters to plain Latin |
| "LE ROY" vs LEROY | Don't force-join split names; match leniently in search |

Prompting "write names exactly as carved" wouldn't stop these.

## Caveat
- With 8 photos, one flipped stone moves the score about 14 points.
- Judge each change by which stone changed and why, not by the percentage.
